metadata.blurb: The self-custody wallet for swapping, sending, bridging, and exploring apps across 16+ networks.

ref.explanation: Uniswap Wallet mobile and extension apps follow EIP-7702 for smart-wallet delegation; new wallets are smart wallets by default while remaining controlled by the user's private key.
Uniswap's Smart Wallet overview documents its EIP-7702 implementation and links the Calibur smart-wallet contract.
Uniswap Wallet lets users create a new Ethereum wallet or import an existing crypto wallet.
Uniswap Labs states that the wallet is self-custodial and that users remain responsible for recovery phrases.
Uniswap documents its smart wallet as the Calibur implementation using EIP-7702 delegation, with users keeping the same EOA address.
Uniswap Wallet security docs describe self-custodial recovery-phrase ownership rather than MPC or Safe account custody.
Uniswap documents its smart wallet as the Calibur implementation using EIP-7702 delegation, with users keeping the same EOA address.

Uniswap Wallet users can claim uni.eth usernames that work anywhere ENS addresses are supported.
ENS's Uniswap case study says the Uniswap Wallet mobile app and browser extension use ENS for human-readable names.
The Uniswap Wallet App Store listing describes swapping across Ethereum, Unichain, Base, BNB Chain, Arbitrum, Polygon, Optimism, and other EVM-compatible chains.
The Uniswap Wallet site describes swap, buy, sell, bridge, send, and receive in one place.
The Uniswap Wallet App Store listing says users can view crypto and NFT assets in one place without switching chains.
The Uniswap Extension page says all tokens appear in one place and users do not need to switch chains to view assets.

The Uniswap Wallet mobile app is explicitly licensed under GPL 3.0 or later. The browser extension directory in the same monorepo does not contain a `LICENSE` file. Development happens in a private repository and only production-ready code is published.

Uniswap Labs raised $165M in a Series B led by Polychain Capital in October 2022, with participation from a16z, Paradigm, SV Angel, and Variant, at a $1.66B valuation. Total funding across all rounds is approximately $176M.
Uniswap Wallet supports multiple wallet addresses under the same recovery phrase and lets users create additional wallet addresses.
Apple's App Store privacy disclosure for Uniswap Wallet lists diagnostics, including crash data and performance data, under data not linked to the user.
Uniswap Labs says it uses anonymous usage data across its products and provides an in-wallet analytics opt-out.
Apple's App Store privacy disclosure for Uniswap Wallet lists product interaction usage data under analytics.

Uniswap Labs support says other people can see a wallet's tokens, NFTs, and transaction history because wallet transaction information is stored and verified on public blockchains and public wallet addresses/transactions are visible through block explorers.
Uniswap Wallet address documentation describes receiving funds through a normal public wallet address or ENS username, not through stealth-address or Privacy Pools recipient flows.

Uniswap Labs support says other people can see a wallet's tokens, NFTs, and transaction history because wallet transaction information is stored and verified on public blockchains and public wallet addresses/transactions are visible through block explorers.
Uniswap Wallet address documentation describes receiving funds through a normal public wallet address or ENS username, not through stealth-address or Privacy Pools recipient flows.
Uniswap Labs runs a bug bounty program through Cantina. The wallet mobile app and browser extension are in scope, with rewards up to $50K for critical wallet vulnerabilities.
Uniswap support says the mobile wallet can require Face ID, Touch ID, or Android biometrics before the app opens or before swaps/transactions are submitted.
CryptoSlate's current Uniswap Wallet product profile lists hardware wallet support as No for the Uniswap Wallet app/extension product.
Uniswap Labs describes Uniswap Wallet as available on iOS, Android, and Chrome; separate hardware-wallet connectivity is documented for the Uniswap web app rather than the Uniswap Wallet app itself.

Uniswap Labs documents the Wallet and Extension as interfaces compatible with a maintained list of supported networks; unsupported-network tokens are not visible in the products, indicating an interface/RPC-backed network model rather than an embedded Ethereum L1 light client.
Uniswap says its smart wallet feature uses EIP-7702 delegation while the wallet remains controlled by the user's private key.
Uniswap Wallet account recovery is documented through the wallet recovery phrase, which can be used to import the wallet into another wallet app.
Uniswap Wallet and Extension may show transaction warnings for unverified contracts and malicious transactions using Blockaid and WalletConnect/ReOwn signals.
Uniswap Wallet and Extension may show connection warnings for malicious, unverified, and verified dapps.
Uniswap Wallet and Extension may display decoded transaction data, token amounts sent or received, and warnings for potentially malicious transactions.

Uniswap Wallet and Extension display decoded transaction data for connected dapp transactions, including token amounts sent and/or received and warnings for unverified or potentially malicious transactions.
Blockaid transaction security simulates and validates transactions in real time so users can understand resulting state changes and outcomes before signing.
Uniswap says Wallet and Extension display decoded transaction data including token amounts being sent and/or received for dapp transactions.
Blockaid describes Transaction Preview as revealing the full onchain impact of a transaction before it is signed, including state changes and outcomes.
Uniswap Labs documents how users can revoke token approvals through block explorers' approval checkers.
Uniswap Labs recommends Etherscan token approvals and Revoke.Cash for checking a wallet's approvals.

Uniswap Labs says its Wallet and Extension are compatible with maintained supported networks and that tokens sent on unsupported networks are not visible in Uniswap Labs products; it does not expose user-selected Ethereum mainnet RPC/self-hosted-node submission in this product model.
Uniswap Wallet publishes a browser extension through the Chrome Web Store.
Chrome for Developers states that all Chrome Web Store extensions are signed by Google, with signing handled automatically when a package is uploaded.
Uniswap Labs publishes version history for the Uniswap Wallet iOS app in the App Store.
The public Uniswap interface repository README states releases are automatically tagged after production-ready code is published.

Uniswap's public interface repository says wallet mobile and extension code is published after private development cycles and releases are tagged, but this publication model is source-available release tagging rather than an independently documented reproducible-build verification process for published wallet artifacts.

Uniswap Wallet security documentation describes the wallet code as source-available for public review, but does not document deterministic rebuild instructions for matching mobile app or browser extension release artifacts.

Uniswap crosschain swap support explicitly lists Solana as not available for crosschain swaps; wallet-level Solana support was not proven.
The Uniswap Wallet supports only EVM chains (Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, etc.) and cannot hold or send native BTC.
The wallet is EVM-only and provides no Cosmos SDK/IBC chain support per its network documentation and reviews.
